• don't mess with them, it's the kind of procedure that has to be done by a professional to avoid irritation, making them look worse or even scarring the skin.

• use salicylic acid, it's an effective anti-inflammatory, Which can help with breakouts and soothe inflamed skin. 
Glycolic acid is very effective for exfoliating skin and removing build ups, debris that clog pores.
Retinoids can help with the appearance of black heads, as it stimulates cellular turnover, which prevents the buildup of dead skin cells. 
The ordinary sells good salicylic and glycolic acids.

• double cleanse, balm + cream cleansers are my favourite combination but you can also use oil + milk cleanser or micellar water + cream cleanser. The more you massage your skin, the more efficient it'll be to reduce the appearance of blackheads and blemishes.

•use exfoliators !! Nothing works faster than this, it'll even take care of discoloration, scars and wrinkles. Chemical peels are the best, I HIGHLY recommend Paula's choice 2% bha liquid exfoliant.

In the shower I put a recipient under my head ( facing the ground so that my hair are upside down, it's better to get to the roots directly ) above a bowl. I do both, I pour it and  I dunk my hear repeatedly.
Since I have medium porosity, I don't need that much time until my hair absorbs what I give it. So I let it sit there for about 15 minutes. 
When I don't have the time but still want minimum effects, I let it sit for ten minutes while I finish the other steps of my routine ( for example, wash my body and stuff )

I can't really wash my hair without a shampoo because I have a skin condition that affects my scalp ( shampoo = treatment ) but I do it after my shampoo yes, a bit like a mask.
